article.title: Second Conditional
article.description: Structure: If + past simple, ... would + base verb. Used for hypothetical or unlikely present/future situations: 'If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.' Common mistake: using 'would' in the if-clause too — 'If I would win the lottery' is incorrect; the if-clause always uses past simple.
article.content: Structure: If + past simple, ... would + base verb. Used for hypothetical or unlikely present/future situations: 'If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.' Common mistake: using 'would' in the if-clause too — 'If I would win the lottery' is incorrect; the if-clause always uses past simple.

generated.caption:
Ever wonder what you'd do if you suddenly became rich? 💭 That's a perfect scenario for the **Second Conditional!**

We use this structure (If + past simple, ... would + base verb) for hypothetical or unlikely present/future situations. A common mistake is using 'would' in the 'if' part – remember, it's always past simple there!

Example: *'If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.'*

slides.body: The Second Conditional is used to talk about hypothetical or unlikely situations in the present or future. Its structure is 'If + past simple, ... would + base verb'. For example, 'If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.' This expresses an unlikely scenario and its potential outcome. Many mistakenly use 'would' in the 'if' clause, saying 'If I would win...', but remember, the 'if' clause always requires the past simple form of the verb, not 'would'.
